title: Working Example of the Story Analysis Workflow Using a Publicly Available Workflow Engine

story.so_that: I can durably automate complete multi-step workflows of agentic action
story.as_a: Software Engineer, and AI Process Designer
story.i_want: a working example of the Story Analysis Workflow of the SDLC process using a publicly available workflow engine

target_persona.name: Alex - Software Engineer & AI Process Designer

journey.before: Alex manually invokes each SDLC skill (extract-story-intent, analyze-story, draft-implementation-plan, etc.) one at a time, hand-tracking state, retries, and an audit trail across the multi-step Story Analysis Workflow.
journey.during: Alex defines the Story Analysis Workflow in a publicly available workflow engine, which durably orchestrates the SDLC skills end-to-end, persisting state, retrying failed steps, and pausing to escalate to a human whenever a step encounters ambiguity or uncertainty.
journey.after: Alex inspects the workflow engine's audit/trace log and the resulting repository changes (created/updated files) to confirm the workflow completed successfully, and reuses or shares the documented workflow definition with other engineers for future stories.

capability_breakdown.core_action: Orchestrate the multi-step Story Analysis Workflow (extract-story-intent, analyze-story, and subsequent SDLC skills) as a single durable workflow in a publicly available workflow engine, including state management, retry-loops, and human-in-the-loop escalation on ambiguity or uncertainty.
inputs: Story document or verbatim story text to seed the workflow
Workflow definition/configuration for the chosen publicly available workflow engine
Human responses when a step escalates due to ambiguity or uncertainty
outputs: Completed workflow run with an auditable, traceable execution log covering every agentic action and tool call
Repository state changes produced by the workflow's agentic actions (e.g., extracted intent JSON, analysis JSON, updated documentation)
Documentation describing how the workflow is built, configured, and run so others can reuse it
state_changes: Repository files created or updated by each agentic action invoked during the workflow
Workflow execution state persisted by the workflow engine (e.g., running, retrying, waiting-for-human, completed, failed)

affected_components.ui: None - no end-user UI; workflow engine's own dashboard/console (if any) is used for observability
affected_components.api: Workflow engine's orchestration API/webhooks used to invoke SDLC skill steps and report step results
affected_components.database: Workflow engine's durable execution/state store used to persist workflow run state, history, and retries
affected_components.external_services: Publicly available workflow engine (e.g., Temporal, Prefect, n8n, or similar) hosting and executing the workflow

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A working example of the Story Analysis Workflow of the SDLC process using a publicly available workflow engine
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the Story Analysis Workflow is defined in a publicly available workflow engine When the workflow is triggered with a story document Then the workflow runs the SDLC Story Analysis steps end-to-end and completes successfully
acceptance_criteria.persona_served: Alex - Software Engineer & AI Process Designer

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The implemented workflow is documented and can be used by others
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the workflow implementation exists When another engineer reads its documentation Then they can configure and run the workflow themselves without additional guidance
acceptance_criteria.persona_served: Alex - Software Engineer & AI Process Designer

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The implemented workflow demonstrates flow of agentic actions, including tool calls and state management, retry-loops, and punching out to the human in cases of ambiguity or uncertainty
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow step fails or encounters ambiguous input When the workflow engine processes that step Then it retries the step according to the retry policy or pauses and escalates to a human for input before continuing
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Trace agentic workflow execution through retries and human escalation
acceptance_criteria.persona_served: Alex - Software Engineer & AI Process Designer

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Workflow actions are auditable and traceable after workflow completion
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow run has completed When Alex reviews the workflow engine's execution history Then every agentic action and tool call taken during the run is visible and traceable
acceptance_criteria.persona_served: Alex - Software Engineer & AI Process Designer

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Agentic Workflow actions affect the repository state (e.g., create files, update documentation)
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the workflow executes its agentic action steps When those steps complete Then corresponding files are created or updated in the repository
acceptance_criteria.persona_served: Alex - Software Engineer & AI Process Designer

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Workflow is repeatable, producing similar results when given the same inputs
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the same story document input is provided When the workflow is run multiple times Then each run produces similar results and repository state changes
acceptance_criteria.persona_served: Alex - Software Engineer & AI Process Designer
